messages:
Anna (Support): Heads-up: customer reported invoice INV-2026-0555 showing CA sales tax (7.25%) even though their account is registered in OH and they have nexus only in OH. They have a PO (PO-9876) on file. Can billing/finance advise? https://app.redwood.example/invoices/INV-2026-0555 :confused:

Liam (Billing): Thanks Anna. Do we have the invoice payload / tax decision log? Also what payment method was used on the invoice? If PO was used, we should be using account billing address for jurisdiction.

Anna (Support): Copying payload from our side (redacted):
```\n{\n  "invoice_id": "INV-2026-0555",\n  "account_id": "acct_8421",\n  "po_number": "PO-9876",\n  "account_billing_address": "123 Commerce Way, Columbus, OH 43215",\n  "payment_method": { "type": "card", "card_last4": "4242", "billing_zip": "94105", "card_country": "US" },\n  "tax_engine_input": { "merchant_nexus": ["OH"], "determination_mode": "default" }\n}\n```

But the tax engine decision says: `applied_rate: 0.0725, jurisdiction: CA, reason: card_billing_zip_fallback`

Sophie (Finance): This looks like a fallback rule kicked in. For PO-backed invoices we explicitly require using `account_billing_address` for tax jurisdiction. If that field existed in the invoice payload the tax engine shouldn't have used card zip. Can you confirm if the invoice builder ever drops `account_billing_address` during PO path?

Mike (Platform Eng): Looking at the invoice-generation path. There's a known conditional where if `payment_method` is present we were passing `billing_location` = `payment_method.billing_zip` into the tax service unless `override_billing_address` is true. PO path sets `override_billing_address` in the UI, but backend was failing to set the flag when `po_number` is present for some customers created before 2024-06.

Mike (Platform Eng): Relevant snippet from router (old logic):
```\nif (payment_method) {\n  billing_location = payment_method.billing_zip\n} else if (account.billing_address) {\n  billing_location = account.billing_address.zip\n}\n```
So payment_method wins even for PO invoices.

TaxBot: Tax decision summary for INV-2026-0555 -> used fallback `card_billing_zip` (94105) -> mapped to CA tax table -> rate 7.25% -> taxable amount $2,400 -> tax $174.00.

Liam (Billing): Ugh. Customer definitely expects taxes per their account address. We need to: 1) issue credit note for the tax amount, 2) patch invoice pipeline to prefer `account_billing_address` when `po_number` is present (and for enterprise customers with `po_required`), 3) run a query for affected invoices in the past 90 days.

Anna (Support): Customer asked for a timeline. They need a corrected invoice and credit ASAP. I've told them we will escalate.

Sophie (Finance): I'll prepare the credit note once engineering confirms the scope of affected invoices. Liam can you run a search for invoices where `po_number` IS NOT NULL and `tax_jurisdiction` == CA but `account_billing_address.state` != CA? Probably something like:
```\nSELECT invoice_id FROM invoices\nWHERE po_number IS NOT NULL\n  AND tax_jurisdiction = 'CA'\n  AND account_billing_address->>'state' != 'CA'\n  AND created_at > now() - interval '90 days';\n```
I'll hold on credits until we have the list.

Mike (Platform Eng): I'll open a PR to change the precedence: `if (po_number) use account.billing_address else fallback to payment_method.billing_zip`. Also adding a feature-flagged rollout so we can toggle if anything breaks. Estimated fix + deploy in next 2 business days.

Anna (Support): Repro steps for ops/eng to validate: 
1) Create test account with `po_required = true` and account billing state = OH.
2) Create invoice with `po_number` set and attach a card with CA billing zip 94105.
3) Run invoice calculation -> verify tax jurisdiction selected.
4) After patch, run same test to confirm tax jurisdiction is OH.

Mike (Platform Eng): Good. I'll run the test locally and post results.

TaxBot: Quick audit note: we flagged 12 invoices across 8 accounts in the last 60 days matching the pattern (po present, tax jurisdiction = CA, account state != CA). List uploaded to /ops/tax-mismatch/1822500000.csv

Liam (Billing): Thanks taxbot. Sophie and I will prepare credits for those 12 and prioritize the current customer first.

Sophie (Finance): I'll file the credit for INV-2026-0555 now and attach a manual note: `Tax applied based on card billing zip due to fallback; issuing credit and corrected invoice. Root cause: invoice pipeline precedence bug.`

Anna (Support): Customer updated: they requested a corrected invoice and confirmation that future invoices won't have the same issue. I confirmed we'll do credits + fix. They asked for an ETA — I'll provide "48 hours" pending engineering confirmation.

Mike (Platform Eng): Local test: before patch -> tax jurisdiction CA (94105), after patch -> OH (43215). Tests green. Patch linked: https://git.redwood.example/infra/invoice/commit/abc123. Rolling out behind flag now.

Sophie (Finance): Credit created for INV-2026-0555 (CN-2026-0091) for $174.00, customer notified. We'll follow up once the flag is fully rolled out to backfill the other invoices.

Liam (Billing): I'll run the backfill script to issue credits for the 12 flagged invoices and coordinate with support for customer comms.

Anna (Support): Closing loop with the customer and marking as escalated -> resolved for now. Will reopen if any customers report issues. :white_check_mark:
